comment: C’s low-rate RMSprop with a deep, two-LN network outperformed both Adagrad E and momentum-SGD B. I overextended K1057’s same-architecture Adam-versus-RMSprop evidence into a general RMSprop penalty, and used K1008’s rectifier tendency across optimizer/residual changes. K1012 correctly warns against such ordering from close progress proxies. RMSprop’s running gradient normalization versus Adagrad’s accumulating denominator is a plausible contributor, not an established cause. Backtesting normalized RMSprop lr≤1e-4 against Adagrad lr≥1e-3 yielded 2/3 history wins and 5/10 lab wins; against momentum-SGD lr≤.001, 2/5 history and 19/34 lab wins. No lab pair matched smooth RMSprop versus rectifier Adagrad. These mixed results do not support a general corrective rule.

        self.act = nn.LeakyReLU(0.01)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        h = self.linear(self.norm(x))
        h = h + x
